test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The intelligence quotients (IQs) of 16 students from one area of a city showed a mean of 107 and standard deviation (sd) of 10 while IQs of 14 students from another area of the city showed a mean of 112 and sd of 8. The null hypothesis to be tested is that there is significant difference between IQs of the two groups. The distribution with degrees of freedom and value of test statistic assuming that null hypothesis is true, are:

options.text: Chi-square distribution with 29 degrees of freedom and 1.89
t distribution with 28 degrees of freedom and 1.45
Chi-square distribution with 25 degrees of freedom and 2.65
t distribution with 25 degrees of freedom and 4.26

solution:
The correct answer is** t distribution with 28 degrees of freedom and 1.45**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Explanation:

__
 
• Degrees of Freedom: The degrees of freedom (df) for a two-sample t-test is calculated as the sum of the sample sizes minus 2. In this case, df = (16 - 1) + (14 - 1) = 28.
 
• The t-distribution is appropriate for comparing the means of two small samples.
 
• **The test statistic value of 1.45 is derived from the formula for the t-test for independent samples.**
 
• The null hypothesis states there is no significant difference between the IQs of the two groups, hence the test statistic under the t-distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Explanation of Incorrect Options:

 
• **Option 1:** Chi-square distribution with 29 degrees of freedom and 1.89

 
 
• The Chi-square distribution is not appropriate for comparing means of two samples.
 
• Degrees of freedom for Chi-square test are typically associated with categorical data, not continuous data like IQ scores.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** Chi-square distribution with 25 degrees of freedom and 2.65
 
 
• Again, Chi-square is not suitable for this type of hypothesis testing.
 
• Degrees of freedom are incorrectly calculated for a Chi-square test in this context.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** t distribution with 25 degrees of freedom and 4.26
 
 
• The degrees of freedom are incorrectly calculated; it should be 28, not 25.
 
• The test statistic value of 4.26 is incorrect based on the given data.
